body:
Reproduced on 4.47 (`chrislusf/seaweedfs:4.47`), through to the completed object becoming unreadable. Two things that may be worth adding here.

It is not only `s3.clean.uploads`. `AbortMultipartUpload` on the leftover upload id does the same: `abortMultipartUpload` removes `.uploads/<id>` with data deletion on (`weed/s3api/filer_multipart.go`). The leftover is listed by `ListMultipartUploads`, so any client or tool that aborts the incomplete uploads it finds there destroys the completed object. Replacing the `s3.clean.uploads` line in the script below with `aws s3api abort-multipart-upload --bucket repro --key obj --upload-id "$upload"` gives the same result. We have not checked whether the S3 lifecycle worker's `AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload` takes the same path.

The damage is invisible until vacuum. Right after the chunks are deleted, GET still returns the whole object with the right MD5, because reads fall back to `readDeleted=true`. It only fails once `volume.vacuum` has compacted the volume, and by then there is nothing left to recover. A check that reads the object in between passes.

On how likely the leftover is: besides a filer error during the post-commit removal, a stop of the S3 server between committing the object and removing `.uploads/<id>` is enough — a SIGKILL from a container runtime whose stop timeout is shorter than the ~20 s the server takes to shut down, for instance.

The repro simulates the leftover by snapshotting `.uploads/<id>` with `fs.meta.save` before completing and restoring it with `fs.meta.load` afterwards, which is the state a failed cleanup leaves. It needs Docker and the AWS CLI.

<details>
<summary>Script</summary>

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# s3.clean.uploads deletes the chunks of a completed object when the upload's
# directory was left behind after CompleteMultipartUpload.
# Needs docker and the AWS CLI.
set -euo pipefail

PORT=18933
export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=any AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=any AWS_DEFAULT_REGION=us-east-1
s3() { aws --endpoint-url "http://localhost:$PORT" s3api "$@"; }
ws() { docker exec seaweedfs-repro sh -c "printf '%s\n' \"\$1\" | weed shell" _ "$1" 2>&1 | { grep -v -e '^$' -e nterprise -e 'which has advanced' || true; }; }

work=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'docker rm -f seaweedfs-repro >/dev/null 2>&1; rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
cd "$work"

docker run --detach --name seaweedfs-repro --publish "$PORT:8333" chrislusf/seaweedfs:4.47 \
  server -s3 -s3.port=8333 -master.volumeSizeLimitMB=64 -volume.max=0 > /dev/null
timeout 90 sh -c "until curl -sf http://localhost:$PORT/status > /dev/null; do sleep 1; done"

s3 create-bucket --bucket repro > /dev/null
head -c 6000000 /dev/urandom > part1
head -c 1000000 /dev/urandom > part2
cat part1 part2 > whole
echo "== object md5: $(md5sum whole | cut -d' ' -f1)"

upload=$(s3 create-multipart-upload --bucket repro --key obj --query UploadId --output text)
etag1=$(s3 upload-part --bucket repro --key obj --upload-id "$upload" --part-number 1 --body part1 --query ETag --output text)
etag2=$(s3 upload-part --bucket repro --key obj --upload-id "$upload" --part-number 2 --body part2 --query ETag --output text)

# Snapshot the upload directory's metadata before completing, so its leftover
# can be put back afterwards.
ws "fs.meta.save -o /data/upload.meta /buckets/repro/.uploads/$upload" > /dev/null

s3 complete-multipart-upload --bucket repro --key obj --upload-id "$upload" \
  --multipart-upload "{\"Parts\":[{\"PartNumber\":1,\"ETag\":$etag1},{\"PartNumber\":2,\"ETag\":$etag2}]}" > /dev/null
s3 get-object --bucket repro --key obj got > /dev/null
echo "== completed; GET md5: $(md5sum got | cut -d' ' -f1)"

# What a crash between committing the object and removing .uploads/<id> leaves
# behind (completeMultipartUpload only logs that removal's failure, at V(1)).
ws "fs.meta.load /data/upload.meta" > /dev/null
echo "== leftover restored; ListMultipartUploads now shows: $(s3 list-multipart-uploads --bucket repro --query 'Uploads[].UploadId' --output text)"

sleep 2
echo "== s3.clean.uploads:"
ws "s3.clean.uploads -timeAgo=1s"

s3 get-object --bucket repro --key obj got > /dev/null
echo "== after s3.clean.uploads; GET md5: $(md5sum got | cut -d' ' -f1)  (served from deleted needles)"

ws $'lock\nvolume.vacuum -garbageThreshold 0.0001\nunlock' > /dev/null
if s3 get-object --bucket repro --key obj got > /dev/null 2> err; then
  echo "== after volume.vacuum; GET md5: $(md5sum got | cut -d' ' -f1)"
else
  echo "== after volume.vacuum; GET fails: $(grep -o 'An error occurred.*' err)"
  docker logs seaweedfs-repro 2>&1 | grep 'GetObjectHandler: failed to stream' | tail -1
fi
```

</details>
